messages:
maya (support): hey, forwarding an Escalation from Acme. They see intermittent embedding failures: dimension_mismatch errors, a bunch of increased latency, and some billing/quota 4xx responses. Happens only for embeddings and seems region-related. sample error: "dimension_mismatch expected 3072 got 1536". They say it spikes when they bulk upload (~200 req/s).

maya (support): their quick repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-large","input":["doc1","doc2", ... ]}'
```
response (snippet):
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  "error": "dimension_mismatch",
  "expected": 3072,
  "got": 1536,
  "request_id": "rwid-7a2b3c"
}
```
They attached request ids and say sometimes it works fine, then bursts of errors. Also says they see calls routed to eu-west when their app is US-only.

cheng (devex): thanks — can you paste the full request_id(s)? also did they include a region header or use a regioned endpoint? we recently changed default routing for free-tier fallbacks.

maya (support): gave us 3 ids: rwid-7a2b3c, rwid-7a2b9f, rwid-7a2c10. No region header in their client, they hit api.redwood.ai (global).

samir (infra-oncall): grabbing logs now. initial look: several of those request_ids hit our US-East router but were overflowed to EU-West pool due to a transient scale event ~1769504250. When we fallback to an alternate pool we sometimes pick a different model variant (small) to keep latency SLOs, which explains 1536 dims vs 3072. This is expected behavior under the cross-region fallback policy but obviously not okay for pinned model semantics.

leo (eng-runtime): yep — root cause: model_variant_fallback + cross-region_spillover. When US pool saturated we route to compatible model in EU pool; the 'compatible' part used to mean feature-equivalent, but for embeddings we treated large/small as compatible (wrong assumption). The runtime returns vector for whatever model actually executed, so client sees dim mismatch.

maya (support): omg. customer pinned model to text-embedding-3-large in the payload (model param). they assumed that guarantees vector shape.

cheng (devex): interim repro so we can test locally:
1) send 200 parallel embedding requests to /v1/embeddings with model=text-embedding-3-large (no region header)
2) watch for any request_id that returns dimension_mismatch
3) if you get one, fetch routing metadata: curl -I + request id to our infra logs (ops has link) to see which pool served it (e.g., us-east-1-pool-3 vs eu-west-2-pool-1).

cheng (devex): quick curl to force region header for testing:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -H "X-Redwood-Region: us-east-1" 
  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-large","input":["a","b"]}'
```
should force US pools — useful to verify whether failures stop.

samir (infra-oncall): mitigation steps I pushed:
- disabled cross-region model_variant_fallback for Acme (customer id provided) at 1769504400
- pinned strict_model_matching=true for their project so any model mismatch returns a clear routing error instead of silently serving smaller variant
- warmed 1x hot instance in US pool to reduce cold starts

ops-bot: note created 9342 (config-change) by samir — change: disabled cross-region fallback for project: acme-prod.

leo (eng-runtime): additional fix tracked: runtime will now compare embedding dims across variant compatibility table BEFORE accepting fallback. If dims differ we won't serve a different-sized embedding; instead the router will either queue (if within latency SLO) or return ROUTING_MODEL_MISMATCH with guidance. patch rolled to staging, PR #1422.

maya (support): customer also saw spikes of billing/429s. is that tied?

samir (infra-oncall): yes a bit. When requests spill to another region they sometimes hit different quota buckets; combined with retries that causes transient 429s. We saw a few requests rejected by EU pool because their account had per-region request limits. I asked billing to unify their quota or bump limits for Acme.

cheng (devex): repro checklist we should give support engineers:
- collect request_id(s)
- ask if they use global endpoint vs regioned one
- ask for model param and confirm model name
- ask client to retry with X-Redwood-Region header to narrow down routing
- if they can't set header, ask to enable strict_model_matching in their project settings (support can flip)
- gather stack traces / latencies around the time window and any 429s

maya (support): I relayed mitigations to Acme (we disabled fallback and warmed US). They reran their batch 5 minutes after change. initial report: errors dropped to 0 for their tests, latency stable. They still want a postmortem and permanent fix.

leo (eng-runtime): we'll ship the compatibility-gating fix to prod tomorrow, and add audit logs to show when a request would have been rerouted to another-size variant. Also will add a router metric for cross-region spillover events so SRE can set alerts.

samir (infra-oncall): follow-up ops items:
- increase reserved capacity for embeddings in us-east for critical customers to avoid spillover during busy windows
- ensure quota harmonization across regions (billing)

maya (support): thanks team — I told Acme: short term we disabled fallback and warmed instances (should be stable), medium term runtime patch will prevent incompatible fallbacks, long term we'll add alerts and capacity planning. asked them to reopen if they see anything else. :thumbsup:

cheng (devex): one more note for docs: update the Embeddings troubleshooting page with a clear entry for "dimension_mismatch due to cross-region/model-variant fallback" + recommended mitigations (pin region header, enable strict_model_matching, contact support to bump reserved capacity).

maya (support): closing loop here unless someone wants to add more. cheers.
